Why Google reviews matter so much for local trades

When a homeowner searches "roofer near me", they see a few businesses with star ratings and review counts. Most will call one of those three without scrolling. Reviews affect where you show up in those map results, and they decide who gets picked once you're there. A business with recent, detailed reviews looks active and trustworthy. One with three reviews from 2021 looks like it might have closed.

The system: ask every time, the same way

You don't need software to start. You need a habit.

  1. Get your review link. Search your business name on Google while signed in to the account that manages your Business Profile. Use the "Ask for reviews" option to copy a direct link, or get a QR code. Save the link in your phone's text replacements so you can paste it in two taps.
  2. Ask the same day the job finishes. That's when the customer is happiest and the job is fresh. Waiting a week cuts your response rate.
  3. Ask in person, then send the link. "Would you mind leaving us a quick Google review? I'll text you the link." People who've said yes out loud follow through more often.
  4. Reply to every review. Thank people by name and mention the job. For a bad review, reply once, calmly, and offer to make it right offline.

A text you can copy

Hi [Name], thanks again for having us out for the [job] today. If you were happy with the work, would you mind leaving a quick Google review? It really helps a small business like ours. Here's the link: [your link]. Thanks! – [Your name], [Business]

Keep it short, personal and specific to the job. Mentioning the job also nudges customers to describe it in their review, which helps other homeowners searching for that service.

Where else to put your review link

  • Your invoices and receipts.
  • A QR code on a card you leave behind or on the truck.
  • Your email signature.
  • Your website, next to your existing reviews.

What not to do

Google's rules are strict, and breaking them can get reviews removed or your profile restricted.

  • Don't offer anything in exchange: no discounts, gift cards or entries into a drawing for leaving a review. Google prohibits incentivized reviews.
  • Don't write reviews for yourself or ask friends and family who weren't customers.
  • Don't only ask the happy ones through a filter that routes unhappy customers elsewhere. Ask everyone, and handle complaints directly.

Make your reviews do more work

Reviews on Google help you get found. Showing them on your own page helps you get chosen, because the customer sees them right next to your phone number. Your page should also link back to your Google profile so happy customers can add theirs.

Common questions

How to get more Google reviews as a contractor: common questions

How do I get a link for customers to leave a Google review?

Search your business name on Google while signed in to the account that manages your Business Profile and use the "Ask for reviews" option to copy a direct review link or get a QR code. Text or email that link to customers so they land right on the review form.

When is the best time to ask a customer for a review?

The same day the job is finished, ideally after asking in person. Customers are happiest and the details are fresh, so they're far more likely to follow through than if you ask a week later.

Can I offer a discount for a Google review?

No. Google prohibits offering incentives such as discounts, free services or gift cards in exchange for reviews. Incentivized reviews can be removed and can put your profile at risk.

How do I respond to a bad Google review?

Reply once, calmly and briefly. Thank them, acknowledge the issue without arguing, and offer to make it right by phone or email. Future customers read your reply as much as the review.
